render --help.out:
Usage: retake render [options] <project> <scenario>

render a capture into a finished video: renders/<scenario>-v<N>.mp4 + .json
(theme, components, captions)

Arguments:
  project            project slug or directory
  scenario           scenario name

Options:
  --run <id>         run id, run directory or "latest" (default: the latest
                     capture of the scenario)
  --theme <name>     render with another theme (a theme name or ./path) instead
                     of the one the run used
  --frame <frame>    frame of every scene: card, browser, laptop, phone, tablet,
                     raw, split or pip (multi-page scenes) or a layout component
                     id
  --vertical         the vertical 9:16 variant (1080×1920, reframed on the
                     cursor and the targets), written as
                     <scenario>-v<N>-vertical.mp4
  --square           the square 1:1 variant (1080×1080, reframed), written as
                     <scenario>-v<N>-square.mp4
  --music <file>     music bed (an audio file: path from here, else relative to
                     the project) instead of the scenario's
  --no-music         leave the scenario's music bed out
  --tutorial         turn every tutorial overlay on (key caps, spotlight, step
                     badges, loupe, progress bar) over the scenario's switches
  --no-tutorial      leave the tutorial overlays out
  --scale <n>        output size multiplier of 1920×1080 (default: the capture
                     scale)
  --no-intro         leave the intro out
  --no-outro         leave the outro out
  --out <file>       write the video (and its .json record) here instead of
                     renders/
  --concurrency <n>  frames rendered in parallel, 1-16 (default: retake.yaml
                     render.concurrency, $RETAKE_RENDER_CONCURRENCY, else 3 on
                     the GPU path, 3/4 of the CPUs in software)
  --json             print the render record (without the plan) as JSON
  --review           review the render right after it (retake review: sheets,
                     key frames, report)
  --no-wait          start at once even while a take films on this Mac (default:
                     wait for it, then go on at background priority during later
                     takes)
  -h, --help         display help for command

still --help.out:
Usage: retake still [options] <project> <scenario>

render one frame of the planned video as a PNG (renders/stills/)

Arguments:
  project           project slug or directory
  scenario          scenario name

Options:
  --frame <n>       output frame number (0-based)
  --run <id>        run id, run directory or "latest" (default: the latest
                    capture of the scenario)
  --layout <frame>  frame of every scene (as `retake render --frame`): card,
                    browser, laptop, phone, tablet, raw, split or pip
                    (multi-page scenes) or a layout id
  --theme <name>    plan with another theme (a theme name or ./path)
  --vertical        a frame of the vertical 9:16 variant
  --square          a frame of the square 1:1 variant
  --out <file>      PNG file to write
  --json            print the result as JSON
  --no-wait         start at once even while a take films on this Mac (default:
                    wait for it, then go on at background priority during later
                    takes)
  -h, --help        display help for command

export --help.out:
Usage: retake export [options] <project> <render>

export a render: mp4_1080p, mp4_4k, webm, vertical_9x16, square_1x1, gif_preview
→ exports/<render>/ + manifest.json

Arguments:
  project            project slug or directory
  render             render id (e.g. quote-v6), a renders/<id>.json or .mp4
                     path, or "latest"

Options:
  --formats <list>   comma-separated formats, or "all" (default:
                     mp4_1080p,webm,gif_preview)
  --scenario <name>  with "latest": the latest render of this scenario
  --out <dir>        output folder (default: exports/<render-id>/)
  --gif-start <s>    start of the GIF preview, seconds (default: around the
                     first marker, else the start)
  --concurrency <n>  frames rendered in parallel by re-rendered formats
  --json             print the export manifest as JSON
  --no-wait          start at once even while a take films on this Mac (default:
                     wait for it, then go on at background priority during later
                     takes)
  -h, --help         display help for command

review --help.out:
Usage: retake review [options] <project> <render>

review a render: contact sheets, per-scene sheets, key frames, timeline and
report in review/<render>/

Arguments:
  project            project slug or directory
  render             render id (e.g. catalogue-v3), a renders/<id>.json or .mp4
                     path, or "latest"

Options:
  --fps <n>          contact sheet frames per second (choices: "1", "2")
  --previous <id>    compare with this render (default: the previous render of
                     the same scenario)
  --no-previous      do not compare with a previous render
  --scenario <name>  with "latest": the latest render of this scenario
  --strict           exit with 1 when the review is not clean (errors or
                     warnings)
  --json             print the review result (report.json) as JSON
  --no-wait          start at once even while a take films on this Mac (default:
                     wait for it, then go on at background priority during later
                     takes)
  -h, --help         display help for command

run --help.out:
Usage: retake run [options] <project> <scenario>

run a scenario headless: capture.mp4 + timeline.json (or a dry run with
screenshots)

Arguments:
  project            project slug or directory
  scenario           scenario name or YAML file

Options:
  --dry              dry run: no video, a screenshot per step, irreversible
                     steps not executed
  --until <ref>      stop after this step (<scene>.<step id|index>, a step id,
                     or a scene id)
  --hooks <mode>     setup/teardown hooks (default: run for captures, skip for
                     dry runs) (choices: "run", "skip")
  --env <name>       environment (default: scenario env, project default_env,
                     first one)
  --headed           show the browser window (needs a display)
  --allow-writes     let a run on a production environment write (only where
                     project.yaml sets access: read-write; without it such a run
                     is read-only)
  --sandbox          reset the sandbox to its seed before the take: up if
                     needed, health, reset (environment: --env, the scenario env
                     or default_env when a sandbox, else the first sandbox); it
                     stays up after
  --json             stream progress events as JSON lines on stdout
  --raw              then export the raw package for editors (as retake
                     export-capture: clips per scene, cursor data, markers)
  --cursor <mode>    with --raw: baked (as captured), none (captured without the
                     cursor; data only) or layer (captured without it + a
                     transparent cursor layer per clip) (choices: "baked",
                     "none", "layer")
  --format <format>  with --raw: mp4 (H.264 high, CRF 14) or prores (ProRes 422
                     HQ) (choices: "mp4", "prores")
  --fps <n>          with --raw: 30 or 60 fps (choices: "30", "60")
  --layer <format>   with --raw --cursor layer: prores (ProRes 4444) or webm
                     (VP9 alpha) (choices: "prores", "webm")
  --selects          with --raw: also one continuous selects file of the clips
  --no-cuts          with --raw: keep the loading inside scenes
  --out <dir>        with --raw: package folder (default
                     exports/<run>-raw-<format><fps>-<cursor>/)
  --no-wait          with --raw: export at once even while another take films
                     (default: wait for it, then yield to later takes)
  -h, --help         display help for command

inspect --help.out:
Usage: retake inspect [options] <project> <page>

replay a page or a scenario (dry, hooks skipped) and list the visible
interactive elements with a target the runner resolves to each, plus a marked
screenshot (what page_inspect gives Claude)

Arguments:
  project            project slug or directory
  page               an environment page key, a URL of one of its pages, or a
                     scenario name (with --until)

Options:
  --env <name>       environment (default: scenario env, project default_env,
                     first one)
  --path <path>      with a page: the path opened under it (default /)
  --until <ref>      with a scenario: inspect after this step (<scene>.<step
                     id|index>, a step id, or a scene id)
  --persona <name>   with a page: sign it in as this persona ("none": signed
                     out)
  --within <target>  list only the elements inside this target (YAML: "{role:
                     dialog}", or text / CSS)
  --target <target>  check a target: matches and the one a step would use
                     (repeatable, ≤ 20)
  --limit <n>        elements listed (default 80, at most 300)
  --images <mode>    marked (default): also draw marked.jpg; none: the plain
                     screenshot only (choices: "marked", "none")
  --json             print the report (inspect.json) on stdout
  --out <dir>        folder for the inspection folder (default
                     <project>/.retake/inspect/)
  -h, --help         display help for command
